c.tagline: The intellectual capital of German Classicism, where Goethe and Schiller once walked and the Bauhaus was born
langs: English (widely spoken in tourist and museum areas)

card: Contactless and card payment are standard at hotels, restaurants, and museums; small cafes and the weekly market may prefer cash, so carry a little euros.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard; the compact Altstadt is largely pedestrian, so taxis drop off at the edge of the historic core

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number and typically reaches English-speaking dispatchers

religion: Unaffiliated/none ~65% (Thuringia is one of Germany's least religious regions)
walk: Highly walkable — the compact Altstadt links Goethe's House, Schiller's House, Theaterplatz, and the Anna Amalia Library within a 15-20 minute walk; Park an der Ilm and Belvedere require a bit more walking or a short bus ride, and Buchenwald is reached by bus or car outside town.

safety.safety: Very safe; Weimar is a low-crime university and heritage town comfortable for solo travelers at any hour
safety.crime: Petty theft is rare; standard caution applies in crowded museum queues and around the train station

hood_landmark.Park an der Ilm: Goethe's Garden House in the landscaped park
hood_landmark.Weimar-West: Modernist residential district (less touristy, everyday Weimar)

hood_desc: The compact historic core packed with Goethe- and Schiller-era landmarks, the Anna Amalia Library, and Theaterplatz — the obvious base for exploring Weimar Classicism on foot.
A sweeping English-style landscaped park along the River Ilm, dotted with follies, Goethe's rustic Garden House, and quiet riverside paths just steps from the Altstadt.
The modern counterpart to Weimar's classical heritage, centered on the Bauhaus Museum and sites tied to the founding of the influential 20th-century design movement.
A quieter residential district west of the center, offering a look at everyday, non-touristy Weimar and more budget-friendly lodging.
The wooded hilltop north of town holding the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial — a solemn, historically vital half-day visit reached by bus.

water.note: German tap water is strictly regulated and safe to drink.

transit.pay: Contactless card, VMT app, or cash on board; day tickets available
transit.map: Route maps at swg-weimar.de and posted at bus stops
transit.note: The Altstadt is fully walkable; buses are mainly useful for Buchenwald, Belvedere, and outlying residential districts

transport.air: Nearest airports are Erfurt-Weimar (ERF), about 20 km / 25 minutes away with limited flights, and Leipzig/Halle (LEJ), a larger option about 1.5 hours away
transport.train: Weimar Hauptbahnhof has frequent regional and ICE connections to Erfurt (~15 min), Leipzig, and Frankfurt
transport.bus: FlixBus and regional coaches connect Weimar to Erfurt, Leipzig, and other German cities; local buses serve Buchenwald and outlying sites
transport.ferry: None — Weimar is inland with no ferry service
transport.car: Reachable via the A4 autobahn; the Altstadt is largely pedestrianized, so park at the edge and walk in

airport.name: Erfurt-Weimar Airport
airport.transport: Taxi transfer roughly €35-45; regional train via Erfurt Hauptbahnhof is a cheaper alternative

net.m: Excellent 4G/5G coverage throughout Weimar and the surrounding Thuringia region
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels, cafes, and most museums
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in cafes and museum lobbies
net.ap: EU roaming covers most European visitors; a prepaid German SIM or eSIM is easy to buy at Leipzig/Halle Airport or a phone shop

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up or a small tip for good service is appreciated
tip.r: 5-10% is customary if service isn't already included — hand the tip directly to the server rather than leaving it on the table
